finding.expected: Preserve the pre-existing canonical TASK identity domain and low-level command compatibility. Pre-resolution synchronization may validate only what is necessary to prove the requested id maps safely to the exact `.ai/tasks/<id>.yaml` path; it must not introduce a new global `TASK-` prefix authority or reuse dispatch-specific identifier policy as canonical TASK-schema policy. Keep malformed/path-like ids fail-closed before network mutation, while safe non-`TASK-` identifiers remain loadable/continuable under the same rules as before TASK-088. Add focused regressions covering a safe non-`TASK-` local task and a safe non-`TASK-` task that exists only upstream, without weakening the new stale-checkout synchronization behavior.
finding.issue: TASK-088 correctly adds the missing-local-TASK pre-resolution sync, but the candidate also changes the global TASK loading contract by importing `TASK_ID_PATTERN` from dispatch reconciliation and requiring every task id to match `^TASK-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`. That restriction is not part of the frozen TASK schema or the pre-TASK-088 `load_task` behavior: canonical TASK parsing accepts a non-empty string task_id, while the prior repository-path guard rejected only empty/path-like ids before loading the exact local file. Because `load_task` is shared by direct run, remediation, repair, state and other low-level paths, this new prefix rule can reject previously valid safe task identities and therefore changes existing command semantics outside the narrow missing-local-TASK `continue` boundary. The new regression even classifies `NOT-A-TASK` as invalid solely because it lacks the `TASK-` prefix, demonstrating the unintended contract narrowing.
